headline: US Third-Quarter GDP Growth Beats Expectations at 3.4% Annualized Rate
summary: The US economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter at an annualized rate of 3.4%. Resilient consumer spending and AI-driven business investment offset the impact of higher oil prices from the Middle East conflict.
why: Gross domestic product is the primary gauge of economic activity, tracking the total value of goods and services produced. Strong GDP growth reassures investors about macroeconomic resilience despite inflationary pressures.

impacts.name: United States
impacts.why: Higher-than-expected GDP growth signals economic strength, which can boost investor confidence in domestic assets.

why_moved: Stronger GDP growth driven by resilient consumer spending and business investment points to robust corporate earnings potential, boosting equity markets.
